hooks.command:
cat <<'HOOK_OUTPUT'
INSTRUCTION: GINI AGENTS CHECK
If this task involves Swift, UIKit, SwiftUI, async/await, actors, Keychain,
networking, testing, App Store submission, or any Gini SDK code:

1. Delegate to the gini-orchestrator agent.
2. gini-orchestrator decides which specialists review: uikit, swiftui, accessibility, testing.
   Architecture, design-system, localization, concurrency, security, performance, and
   background-execution standards still apply and are enforced inline (specialists paused).
3. Do NOT write UI code without mobile-a11y-specialist review.
4. Ensure concurrency safety (data races, actor isolation, @MainActor) — enforced inline.
5. Follow CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md standards: MVVM + Coordinator, design-system
   namespaces (UIColor.GiniBank/GiniCapture, GiniColor, textStyleFonts, Constants),
   3-level localization with typed LocalizableStringResource, /** */ and /// doc
   style, one-parameter-per-line initializers.
6. NEVER create placeholder or stub implementations in production code. Use built-in
   features. Test mocks ARE allowed and required per CLAUDE.md: manual protocol
   conformances, test data from JSON fixtures in Tests/Resources/.
7. Shared rule set: .claude/rules/mandatory-rules.md.

If the task does not involve Swift or Apple platform code, proceed normally.
HOOK_OUTPUT

cat <<'HOOK_OUTPUT'
VALIDATION: Before presenting specialist output to the user:
- Check for conflicts between specialist recommendations
- Verify accessibility was reviewed for user-facing UI code
- Verify design-system and localization rules were applied to UI code
- Reject placeholder or stub implementations in production code (test mocks as
  manual protocol conformances per CLAUDE.md are allowed and expected)
HOOK_OUTPUT
